items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: That's when I -- yeah. Mamie Smith -- and from then on I have recorded, and after making records with her the following summer I went on the road with her.

ctx.x: This must have been 1920. 1920. Because Mamie Smith had made her "Right Here for You" and "Crazy Blues" -- I didn't make that with Mamie. A "Good Man is Hard to Find" -- yeah. I made "Right Here for You" and "Crazy Blues", but she had already had two sides out in 1920, being the first Negro woman to sing on record -- the first blues --
I see. Can you tell us a little about -- what was recording like during the period of your first recording with the Bellhops?
